name: Keratin smoothing treatment

lead: Keratin smoothing, also called a Brazilian keratin treatment or Brazilian blowout, is a salon procedure that reduces frizz, loosens curl and adds shine. Results are visible right away and last a few months, for a sleeker head of hair.

A keratin-based solution is applied and sealed in with a flat iron. Per Grokipedia, hydrolyzed keratin coats and fills the cuticle and heat seals it, mainly altering surface and hydrogen-bond interactions, while formaldehyde-based versions rely on cross-linking. The sources reviewed contain no clinical trials of appearance results.

paras: It is done in a salon in one long session, with results fading over several months. The method emerged in Brazil in the early 2000s and reached the United States around 2006.

Formaldehyde-releasing formulations can irritate eyes, nose and throat, and a 2014 study measured elevated formaldehyde in some products. Wikipedia advises against use during pregnancy, and overuse can cause dryness or breakage.

angle.text: A salon keratin treatment straightens frizz and adds shine, with results visible right away and lasting a few months. Users choose it for a sleeker head of hair; the smoothing is the cosmetic effect itself.

lead: A keratin smoothing treatment, also called a Brazilian keratin treatment or Brazilian blowout, is a salon procedure in which a keratin-based solution is applied to hair and sealed in with heat, with the aim of reducing frizz, adding shine and loosening curl. Results are described as semi-permanent, typically lasting a few months.[1][2]

Wikipedia groups keratin or Brazilian treatments with permanent and semi-permanent straightening methods and describes them as coating hair with keratin and then flat-ironing it, with effects fading over several months.[2] Grokipedia says the method emerged in Brazil in the early 2000s and reached the United States around 2006.[1]

The main documented concern is formaldehyde: a 2014 cross-sectional study in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology examined formaldehyde concentrations in Brazilian keratin-type products, and a 2021 pilot study measured volatile organic compounds among hairdressers in salons serving women of color.[3][4] Wikipedia advises against keratin treatments during pregnancy because some release gases.[2]
infobox: Brazilian keratin treatment, Brazilian blowout, escova progressiva[1]

paras: The procedure applies a formula to the hair, followed by heat from a flat iron to seal it in. Grokipedia describes the aim as smoothing the cuticle, reducing frizz and styling time, and preserving some natural movement rather than fully straightening hair.[1] Wikipedia distinguishes keratin treatments from chemical relaxers, which break the disulfide bonds that give hair its shape, and from Japanese thermal reconditioning.[2]

Per Grokipedia, early formulations combined hydrolyzed keratin with high concentrations of formaldehyde, which acted as a cross-linking agent, and the chemistry drew on textile methods from the 1960s. The Brazilian Blowout brand, introduced in 2005, became the best-known product.[1] The treatment spread internationally from Brazilian salons beginning in the mid-2000s.[1]

Formaldehyde-releasing agents can cause eye, nose and throat irritation during application, and long-term exposure raises questions.[1] A 2014 cross-sectional study reported elevated formaldehyde concentrations in some Brazilian keratin-type products.[3] Studies of hair salon air and hairdresser biomonitoring have measured volatile organic compounds in these settings.[4][5]
Formaldehyde-free alternatives exist and are described as possibly giving less dramatic smoothing and shorter durations.[1] Overuse or high heat can cause dryness or breakage.[1]

Keratin treatments appear in hair-style discussion on looksmaxxing forums, for example in threads from people with curly or coily hair asking how to achieve a straighter-wavy look, where chemical relaxers are suggested as an alternative.
No studies found of keratin smoothing treatments for appearance outcomes. Related research is limited to product formaldehyde measurements and salon exposure studies, described above.[3][4][5]

timeline.event: Keratin smoothing treatments emerge in Brazil.[1]
Treatment first appears in the United States.[1]
